subject: quality
question:
The v2 batch card v2b-lg-01 has 18 functions and runs with `author.py run --no-packet`. It parked with no result. The reason is "no_change: context split with no change (round 1): context split: prompt 110181 tokens > 100000 (turn 26)" (/data/parity-v2/v2batch/results/v2b-lg-01.author.log). The session used 1,832,262 gross tokens (417,607 cost units) and gave 0 MATCH. Two rules caused this result. (1) Round 1 splits into shards only when a packet exists (author.py:1229-1230). The packet is LobbyDaemon-only (author_packet.py:38, ENGINE-ISSUES.md #1), so the batch uses --no-packet and every card runs as one session. (2) split_next parks the card when the session before the split changed no file (author.py:1027-1028). Answer these questions:
(a) Read the session log in /data/parity-v2/v2batch/logs/v2b-lg-01/ (session-01-*.jsonl). Give the prompt tokens after each turn. Put each tool result into one class: card text, evidence/<Exe>/<rva>.txt, pseudocode, source Read, Grep/lessons.md, pdbq. Give the tokens per class. Give the number of functions the agent read before turn 26. Did it start an edit?
(b) Do the same for v2b-pod-01 (23 functions; it split with a handoff, handoff-01-x01.md) and v2b-cg-01 (11 functions; it reached a round-1 build). Do function count, card size in tokens or evidence tokens predict which card hits the split before its first edit?
(c) Is the no_change park correct when no edit was made because the agent was still reading? The docstring says "a fresh session would read the same facts again". Does the handoff text (handoff_text) keep the facts the agent already read, so the next session does not read them again?
(d) Propose one deterministic fix and give its file:line. Options: shard --no-packet cards by function count or by evidence tokens from the card table; a split budget per function; or allow one split with no change when the handoff names the functions already analysed. Estimate the tokens that the fix saves per card for the 6 batch cards (162 items).
why: The v2 batch is the current path to more MATCHes in the 4 other exes. Its first finished card spent about 1.83 M tokens and made no edit. The cause is in the engine, not in the card: without a packet there are no shards, and the no-change park cuts off a session that was still reading. The two large stop-list cards are next: v2b-shared-01 (60 items, 55,045 bytes ≈ 14 k tokens of card text) and v2b-crypto-01 (35 items). They will probably fail the same way ❓. The data shows how many functions fit in one session before 100 k prompt tokens. That gives a real card-size limit and a shard rule for --no-packet cards. It also shows if the no_change park rule is wrong for cards that are still reading. This improves card selection and gives more MATCHes for each token.
answer:
## Corrections to the premise

- `v2batch/logs/` has only the lg-01 log. The pod-01 and cg-01 session logs are in `/data/parity-v2/author/lift-lobbydaemon-v2b-{pod,cg}-01/`. Their `results/*.author.log` files are 0 bytes, because those runs are still running.
- The `### N.` evidence headings give 17 functions for lg-01, 20 for pod-01 and 10 for cg-01. HANDOFF.md gives 18, 23 and 11, because those counts also include the misses.
- The class "evidence/<Exe>/<rva>.txt" has 0 reads in all 4 sessions. With --no-packet, the card md already holds the evidence inline (`## Evidence` section). So the evidence is part of the start prompt, not of the tool results.
- cg-01 reached a build and a compare. The compare gave gain 0 and lost 0, but it reads LobbyDaemon only (ENGINE-ISSUES #2). So this run has no MATCH data for the 4 exes yet.

## Method

- **Prompt per turn:** input + cache_read + cache_creation of each new assistant message id.
- **Class tokens:** I split the real growth from turn k to turn k+1 over the tool results of turn k, by byte share. These numbers include the model's hidden reasoning of that turn.
- **Start prompt:** a fit over the three prompts gives start ≈ 6.4k + 0.583 tokens per prompt byte (about 1.7 bytes per token). The `author_packet.tokens()` estimate (2.5 bytes per token) is about 30 % too low for card md text.

## (a) v2b-lg-01: 26 turns, no Edit, no Write

**Prompt tokens per turn:** 30071, 31050, 31473, 32412, 32871, 33800, 55058, 59284, 62591, 63836, 68315, 69124, 69672, 73330, 77937, 80595, 84308, 86812, 88674, 90351, 92241, 95144, 95747, 96003, 99417, 110181.

The card text is 35,973 bytes, about 21k tokens of the 30k start prompt.

**Growth by class (80,110 tokens in total):**

| Class | Tokens |
| --- | ---: |
| Pseudocode (Read and Grep in hr/) | 22.9k |
| Source Read | 21.8k |
| Grep in src | 17.7k |
| lessons.md | 6.0k |
| pdbq | 5.2k |
| git show | 3.7k |
| ls | 2.8k |
| evidence/*.txt | 0 |

- One turn (T6) cost 21.3k tokens. It read LobbyGate.c lines 100-620 and LobbyGate.cpp lines 1-600 in full.
- The agent touched 16 of the 17 functions (by name or RVA in its tool calls) before turn 26.
- It read the bodies of only about 9 of them. These were the LobbyGate.c and LobbyDPacketHandler.c ranges.
- It did not start an edit. At T26 it was still reading (`Grep Send|encrypt` in Session.h).

## (b) pod-01 and cg-01

| Card | Funcs | Card bytes | Start | First Edit (turn / prompt) | End |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- | --- |
| cg-01 | 10 | 23,350 | 22,087 | T7 / 43,415 | ok at T15 / 61,452 |
| pod-01 s1 | 20 | 38,853 | 31,127 | T9 / 53,509 | split at T27 / 102,967 (4 files changed) |
| pod-01 x01 | 20 | – | 36,486 | T26 / 84,294 | ok at T31 / 96,724 |
| lg-01 | 17 | 35,973 | 30,071 | none | split at T26 / 110,181 |

**Growth by class:**

| Session | Main classes |
| --- | --- |
| pod s1 | Grep in src 39.4k, source Read 9.7k, pseudocode 9.7k, Edit 5.6k |
| pod x01 | source Read 14.4k, Grep 12.8k, lessons 9.1k, git show 4.5k, pseudocode 4.3k |
| cg | pseudocode 8.2k, lessons 7.1k, ls 6.9k, source Read 6.8k, Grep 6.6k |

**Growth per function:**

| Card | Growth per function |
| --- | --- |
| cg-01 | 3.9k (with edits) |
| lg-01 | 4.7k (with no edits) |
| pod-01 (s1 + x01) | 6.6k |

**Predictors:** function count, card tokens and evidence tokens do not predict the park.

- pod-01 is larger than lg-01 on all three measures: 20 against 17 functions, 38.9k against 36.0k card bytes, and 31.8k against 30.3k evidence bytes.
- pod-01 still made its first edit at T9. lg-01 made none.
- The difference is the agent's behaviour (edit early or read everything first), and this is not deterministic.
- With 3 samples, only one rule is safe: start prompt + about 6.6k × functions must stay below the split. A card over about 10 functions does not fit one session. Both lg-01 (17) and pod-01 (20) split.

## (c) The no_change park and the handoff

**The park is wrong for a session that was still reading.** The session made no edit, but it collected facts. The lg-01 park threw away 417,607 cost units.

**The handoff does not keep the facts.** `handoff_text` (author.py:1042-1067) writes only these items:
- the split reason
- the commit sha
- the git numstat
- whether the handoff file exists
- the last 12 tool calls as one-line labels

It holds no function list and no findings. pod handoff-01-x01.md is 1,507 bytes, about 0.9k tokens. So the docstring at author.py:1022 ("a fresh session would read the same facts again") is true.

pod x01 shows this:
- It read 6 of the 20 files of s1 again (PostOfficeDaemon.cpp, PostOfficeDaemon.c, Db.cpp, CMakeLists.txt, lessons.md and the hr/ dir).
- It touched 11 card functions in its first 4 turns.
- Its first Edit came only at T26. About 74 % of its 430,735 units (about 319k) went before that edit.

So a grace split alone does not stop the re-reads.

## (d) Fix: card shards for --no-packet cards

The --no-packet rounds need shards that the driver builds without a model.

1. Add `author_packet.card_shards(card_text, max_funcs)` next to `filter_card` (author_packet.py:274).
   - It splits the card at the `### N. EXE \`rva\` \`name\`` evidence headings.
   - Each shard keeps the card header and the rules, and the evidence of at most k functions. The rows for the other functions are replaced by a one-line note.
   - The ID_ROW filter in filter_card matches no row of the v2b cards (count = 0), so a new filter is necessary.
2. In `s_packet` (author.py:900), when `packet` is false, set `self.packet = {'shards': card_shards(...), 'tokens': ...}`. Use the card filter, not `filter_card`.
3. Then the existing condition at author.py:1230 and the shard loop at :1232-1252 run unchanged.

**Size rule:** choose k so that start(k) + 6.6k·k ≤ 80k.
- start(k) ≈ 6.4k + 0.583 × (template 3.56k bytes + card head + evidence bytes of the k functions).
- For lg-01 this gives k ≤ 8.

| Card | Functions | Shards |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| cg-01 | 10 | 2 |
| pod-01 | 20 | 3 |
| lg-01 | 17 | 3 |
| scd-01 | 14 | 2 |
| crypto-01 | 35 | 5 |
| shared-01 | 56 | 7 |

The no_change park at :1027-1028 stays unchanged. A shard of 8 or fewer functions should reach its first edit before 100k: cg-01 had its first edit at 43k with 10 functions.

**Gain per card (❓ estimates):**

- **lg-01:** the fix avoids the 418k units of the parked session, and the card gets edits.
- **pod-01:** the fix avoids about 319k units of re-reading in x01.
- **crypto-01 and shared-01:** each is likely to split ❓. Their start prompts are about 27k and about 40k tokens, which leaves room for only about 11 and 9 functions. The fix avoids a probable 300-420k waste per card ❓.
- **cg-01 and scd-01:** no saving. Each extra shard costs about 15-25k units of repeated start prompt.

| Scope | Units saved |
| --- | ---: |
| 6 cards (162 items) | about 1.0-1.5 M |
| Mean per card | about 170-250k |

The main gain is in output. All 5 cards with more than 10 functions should give edits in place of a 0-edit park.

proposal:
## Shard --no-packet cards by evidence headings, at most 8 functions per shard

1. **New function:** add `card_shards(card_text, max_funcs=8, budget=80000)` in parityctl/author_packet.py next to `filter_card` (line 274).
   - It parses the `### N. EXE \`rva\` \`name\`` headings in `## Evidence`. It also parses the matching rows of `## Functions in scope` and `## Misses`.
   - It packs functions in card order. A shard closes when it has `max_funcs` functions, or when 6.4k + 0.583 × shard bytes + 6.6k × functions > budget.
   - Each shard keeps the card head (goal, rules, batch notes) and only its own evidence blocks. It adds one line: "(N functions of this card are not shown. Another session does them.)".
   - It returns `{n, modules: [names], rvas, text, tokens}`, so the shard loop does not change.
2. **Driver change:** in author.py `s_packet` (line 900), when `packet` is off, set `self.packet = {'shards': card_shards(self.text), 'tokens': …, 'kind': 'card'}`.
3. **Prompt change:** in `s_session` (author.py:978-983), give the shard text as the card text. Do not use `filter_card` plus a packet for a card shard. `prior_work()` already gives the files of the earlier shards (PRIOR_TOKENS 7000).
4. **No change:** author.py:1230-1252 and the no_change park at :1027-1028 stay as they are.

**Expected gain (❓ estimates):**

- **lg-01:** a 3-shard run replaces a 417,607-unit park with no edit. Each shard costs about 150-200k units, like cg-01 (197k for 10 functions).
- **pod-01:** the fix removes the about 319k-unit re-read in the x01 split.
- **crypto-01 (35 functions) and shared-01 (56 functions):** each card gets 5 or 7 sessions below 80k. This avoids a probable 300-420k-unit park per card ❓.
- **Batch total:** about 1.0-1.5 M cost units saved over the 6 cards (162 items), and all 162 items get an author session with an edit.

**Test:** run lg-01 again. The fix works if each shard session makes its first Edit before 80k prompt tokens and no split fires.

grade.lesson: A --no-packet card never gets shards (author.py:1230 needs self.packet), and handoff_text (author.py:1042-1067) keeps no function list or facts, so a card with more than about 10 functions must be sharded from its "### N." evidence headings before round 1.
grade.notes: Verified these claims. (1) The lg-01 log has 26 turns. The prompt per turn matches exactly, from 30071 to 110181. The only tools are Bash, Grep and Read, so there was no Edit. (2) The state.json rounds match: lg split 26/110181/417607; pod split 27/102967/391243 then ok 31/96724/430735; cg ok 15/61452/197237. (3) handoff-01-x01.md is 1507 bytes. (4) author.py:1027-1028 is the no_change park, and the docstring is at :1022. handoff_text has only the reason, sha, numstat, handoff flag and recent calls. :1230 gates shards on self.packet. s_packet returns 'off' with no packet. (5) The heading counts are 10/20/17/14/35/56 and the card bytes match. (6) The premise corrections are true: logs/ holds only lg-01, and the pod and cg author.log files are 0 bytes. I did not check the per-class token split, the re-read count in pod x01 or the 6.6k-per-function fit. The savings are rough estimates and are marked ❓. The fix is concrete and deterministic, and it reuses the existing shard loop. One risk is not covered: shards of one card share files (for example LobbyGate.c), so a later shard can read the same source again.

subject: tokens
question: In the v2b batch, the context split (CTX_SPLIT = 100,000 prompt tokens, parityctl/author.py:123) and the "split with no change parks no_change" rule (author.py:1027-1028) work together, and together they threw away a full session. Card v2b-lg-01 (18 items) made 42 tool calls (Grep 23, Read 10, Bash 9) and no Edit. It hit the split at turn 26 with a 110,181-token prompt, and it parked no_change after 417,607 cost units (results/v2b-lg-01.author.log). The card prompt is large: prompt-01.md is 1,357 lines, because the batch runs `author.py run --no-packet` and puts the evidence into the card md. Answer these: (1) For the 4 v2b session files under /data/parity-v2/author/*/session-*.jsonl, find the start prompt size in tokens (the first assistant message's input + cache_read + cache_creation). Find the turn and the prompt size at the first Edit or Write, and the cost units spent before it. (2) Split the context at the split point into prompt-01.md, Grep results, Read results and Bash results. Use tokens of the tool_result blocks. (3) Find how many tokens per item the card md uses (cards/v2b-*.md against the item count in HANDOFF.md), and how much context is left for work below 100k when the card has 18, 23, 60 or 35 items. ## (3) Triage design: detail.inline_dir
The rule runs after triage.py:208. It looks only at the direct callees in detail.missing and detail.extra:

1. If extra has `import:abort` and a missing callee has no lift body, set `stub`.
2. If a missing callee has a body in the lift image (same exe and build) **and** the caller source names that callee, set `lift_inlined`.
3. If an extra callee has a lift body and the original does not call it at this site, set `orig_inlined`. Add `scope=global` when the original image has no body of the callee, else `scope=site`.
4. Wrapper test: if the lift body of the extra callee calls the missing callees, set `orig_inlined` (items 103, 217, 60). If the original body of the missing callee calls the extra callees, set `lift_inlined`.
5. If only `qword ptr [reg+N]` or import entries are left, set `indirect`. Else set `true_missing`.
6. Set cross_exe_split for the call family too. Use the caller status in the other exes and in NOREF. Today SPLIT_CAUSES at triage.py:67 holds only the layout and register causes.

I measured steps 1–3 and 5, which use only the image data: they agree with my manual classes on **27 of 40**. The 13 misses need step 4 (wrapper test) or the source grep. That rule is not run yet ❓.

subject: ops
question:
Can a usage limit or a busy slot during `landq recover` park a good card that already started integrate?

Path to check (one recovery after a crash during a land):
1. operator_run.landq_step sees a RUNNING entry with a free lock. It queues 'recover' (operator_run.py:868-869). It adds 1 to `landq_recovers` before the child starts (operator_run.py:886-887). The maximum is `landq_recover_max` = 3 (operator_run.py:96).
2. Lander.recover does not call quota.check first. Lander.run does (landq.py:461). recover goes straight to recover_steps (landq.py:571).
3. When integrate has started, recover_steps runs `cardrun land --approve` (landq.py:598-599). A limit exit 79 raises Waiting (landq.py:720-723). recover_steps turns Waiting into EntryStop('RUNNING', 'recover paused ...') (landq.py:600-601). This drops the structured `limit`. Exit 75 (slot busy) also gives RUNNING (landq.py:607-608).
4. When the child ends with RUNNING, landq_step uses the QUEUED/RUNNING branch (operator_run.py:844-846). That branch sets `landq_not_before = now + 300 s`. It does not use limit_until(). Only WAITING goes to the W9 branch, which has "no retry count" (operator_run.py:847-851).
5. After 3 recovers, the card parks with the text "a dead lander ... did not settle it" (operator_run.py:807-811). The text does not mention a limit.

Sub-questions:
(a) Do two limit hits plus one busy slot in a row park a card whose main push may be very close? Is that the landq form of ops L2/L3 (gap 16: a limit never parks a good card)?
(b) If the limit text has no PAUSE file (ops L2), does the next recover start 300 s later, before the reset time, and use up the budget faster?
(c) Does any unit test or canary mode cover "recover paused" or the `landq_recovers` limit? grep found no test that uses "recover paused".
(d) Smallest fix: should recover_steps raise Waiting, and should drive() map it to WAITING with the limit? Or should landq_step count only recovers that end without 'recover paused' or busy?
why: Ops L2-L5 cover how sched and cardrun count limits and crashes. No lesson covers the landq crash-recovery loop. That loop runs exactly when unattended operation needs it: after a crash during integrate, which is the most dangerous land state. The evidence shows that the recover path counts a pause and a busy slot as failed recovers. The recover delay ignores the limit reset time. The park text then blames a "dead lander", so the operator gets a wrong diagnosis. The fix is small and clear. Option 1: keep Waiting as WAITING with the `limit` in recover_steps, and add a quota.check at the start of recover(). Option 2: count only recovers that really fail in landq_step. Then add a landq unit test and a canary mode (kill during integrate, plus a stub land that exits 79) to keep the fix in place.
answer:
## Short answer

**Yes, a good card can park.** The more likely cause is a busy slot, not a usage limit. The landq recover loop counts a "recover paused" result and a "slot busy" result as failed recovers. After 3 such results, the card parks with the wrong diagnosis "a dead lander". No live run has hit this yet: the live `/data/parity-v2/landq/log.jsonl` has 6 events (5 manual-landed, 1 import-md) and 0 recover events.

## The path, confirmed

| Step | Code | Behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | operator_run.py:868-869, 885-887 | The operator queues 'recover' while `landq_recovers < 3`. It adds 1 **before** the child starts. |
| 2 | landq.py:562-578 | `recover()` does not call `quota.check`. Only `run()` does (landq.py:461, 513). |
| 3 | landq.py:598-602 | Exit 79 from cardrun land is caught as `Waiting`. The code turns it into `EntryStop('RUNNING', 'recover paused …')`, and `w.limit` is lost. |
| 4 | landq.py:607-608 | Exit 75 also gives RUNNING. |
| 5 | landq.py:1197 | The recover CLI returns rc 79 for a pause and rc 75 for busy. These codes are distinct, but the operator ignores rc. |
| 6 | operator_run.py:844-846 | A RUNNING result takes the QUEUED/RUNNING branch: wait 300 s, no `limit_until`, no undo of the count. |
| 7 | operator_run.py:807-811 | When `landq_recovers >= 3`, the card parks with "a dead lander … did not settle it". |

## Sub-questions

**(a) Yes, the card parks. It is the landq form of gap 16, but busy is the main trigger.**
- A usage limit is rare here. Cardrun land returns exit 79 only from the start check at cardrun.py:1648. The land steps skip `quota.check` (cardrun.py:524-526). The operator also starts no recover while it is paused (operator_run.py:859-860). So a limit hit needs a race: another slot writes the PAUSE file in the few seconds between the operator tick and the start of cardrun.
- A busy slot is more likely. landq runs cardrun through `subprocess.run` with no new session and no timeout (landq.py:342). Cardrun holds the slot flock itself (cardrun.py:385-391).
- Scenario: the lander alone gets SIGKILL (for example, the OOM killer). Its cardrun land child lives on, holds slot 4 and may still be pushing. Each recover then gets exit 75. Three busy results take about 2 × 300 s plus run time, so about 10 minutes, and then the card parks.
- A hung step can hold a slot for much longer than that: tools L5 measured 2,654 s and 5,524 s.

**(b) No. The faster-burn case cannot happen in this path.**
- `quota.check` reads only the PAUSE file. So cardrun land cannot return exit 79 when no PAUSE file exists. The ops L2 case (a limit text that only `quota.classify` knows) does not reach this path.
- When a PAUSE file exists, `pause_state` blocks new recovers until the pause ends (operator_run.py:417-431). By then, the 300 s delay has passed.
- What remains: each race still costs 1 of the 3 recovers, and the `limit` is dropped.

**(c) The tests do not cover this. One test even fixes the wrong behaviour in place.**
- tests/test_operator.py:314-323 (`test_recover_that_never_settles_parks_after_the_cap`) uses the stub mode `stay`. That mode means "stays RUNNING, **exit 75**" (tests/operator_stubs.py:12, 133). The test expects a park. So a busy slot that parks the card is the behaviour under test.
- No test uses "recover paused".
- test_landq.py:406-454 tests only the outcomes ok, queued, landed and refused.
- The canary has only `--chaos pause,kill` (canary.py:25-26). It kills the operator, not the lander, and it was last changed at f408e674, before the ef285e73 landq change.

**(d) The smallest safe fix is in the operator.**
- I advise against putting WAITING into recover. The docs say a WAITING entry "lands like QUEUED" (landq.py:31-32). That would send a card whose integrate has already started back through the land steps. ❓ I did not check whether the land steps handle an open intent safely.

## Proposal

**1. landq.py, about 5 lines**
- In `recover_steps` (landq.py:601), set `e['limit'] = w.limit` before you raise RUNNING. This keeps the limit on the entry.
- At the start of `recover()`, add a `quota.check()` call. If it raises `quota.Pause`, return a paused RUNNING result and change nothing.
- ❓ Check that `set_state` keeps the extra keys.

**2. operator_run.landq_step, at lines 844-846, about 15 lines**
- When `proc['cmd'] == 'recover'` and rc is 79: take 1 off `landq_recovers`. Set `landq_not_before = max(now + 300, limit_until(e.limit))`. Copy `limit` to the card.
- When rc is 75: take 1 off `landq_recovers` and add 1 to a new counter, `landq_recover_busy`.
- Park on busy only when the slot has been busy for longer than a set time, for example 2 h. The park text must say "slot N busy since T", not "dead lander".
- Add the entry's last `why` to the park text at line 809.

**3. Tests, about 60 lines**
- Split the stub `stay` into three modes: `busy` (exit 75), `paused` (exit 79 with a limit) and `stay` (exit 2, still RUNNING).
- Expect no park for `paused` and `busy`.
- Expect a park after the cap only for `stay`.
- Add a test_landq case: Waiting during a recover keeps `e['limit']`.

**4. Canary**
- Add a chaos mode `kill-lander`: open the intent, SIGKILL only the landq pid, and keep a stub cardrun alive on slot 4 for about 900 s. Then write a PAUSE file once. Assert that the card ends LANDED and never parks.

**Expected gain:** this closes gap 16 for the land recover path. A good card whose push may be about to finish no longer parks after about 10 minutes because of a busy slot or a pause. The cost is about 20 lines of code and about 60 lines of tests. The gain is preventive, because the live run has done 0 recovers so far.

answer:
## Corrections to the question

- There are 22 helpers, not 19. `fix6_bench.py:185` is one more, and `toolslane.py:82` only wraps `proof.git`.
- `opstatus.py:81` is not the only lock-free reader. `import_state.py:26` passes `--no-optional-locks`. `reclaim_plan.py:50` sets `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0`. `retention.py:67` sets it too.
- `repair.py:202` keeps the tail (300 chars), like `author.py`. `pilot.py:330` keeps the last 400 chars of stderr. `land86.py:170` keeps the first 200 chars.
- `proof.py` does not lose stderr in practice. Its caller at `cardrun.py:755-756` decodes `exc.stderr`. Stderr is lost only for `guard.py`: `cardrun.py:1415` and `cardrun.py:1553` use `str(exc)[:200]`, and `landq.py:547` uses `'%s: %s' % (type, exc)`.
- `slotq.py` and `web.py` contain 0 git calls (checked with grep).

## (a) The helpers

The call counts come from grep for `git(` without the `def` line. `caller` means the helper merges the `env=` that the caller gives.

| author.py:182 | caller | no | RuntimeError | tail 300 | str / CP | 26 | no: own clone (author.py:886) |
| buildonce.py:87 | inherit | no | CalledProcessError, stderr not in message | lost | str | 4 | **yes**: `status` on the lift (buildonce.py:106) |
| canary.py:105 | IDENT + caller | no | Refused | head 300 + repo | str / CP | 20 | no: sandbox |
| cardrun.py:255 | caller | no | StepFail | head 300 | str / CP | 28 (+5 raw `subprocess` calls at 666, 673, 1190, 1444, 1537) | **yes**: `status` on target (cardrun.py:1195); it also writes target (1447 read-tree, 1536-1563 add/commit/push) |
| clientrun.py:78 | inherit | no | Fail | head 300 | str | 4 | ❓ |

## (d) The checker-digest cost

`proof.CHECKERS` (proof.py:63-65) holds strict, cfgcheck, **proof**, **guard**, funcdiff_cached, objcache, buildcache, **buildonce**, linked_build_main.sh, linked_build_noref.sh, gate_full.sh, gate_fast.sh and **toolslane**.

The digest is part of the keys for precheck, full_build and proof (cardrun.py:1212-1219). Review reuse checks it (cardrun.py:892). integrate refuses an old digest (integrate.py:189).

So an edit to guard.py or proof.py forces a new full_build on every card (one example took 435 s on slot4 gap-07) and a new review. There are 33 card directories now.

There is also a trap. If guard, proof, buildonce or toolslane import a new `gitx.py`, then an edit to gitx changes checker behaviour, but the digest does not change. The only fix is to add gitx to CHECKERS, and then each gitx edit forces a full rebuild.

**Verdict:** a change to guard.py or proof.py is not worth the cost now. (b) and (c) show no harm. The one real loss of guard stderr can be fixed at its callers, which are not checkers.

proposal:
**What to add.** Add a new module `parityctl/gitx.py`. Do NOT add it to CHECKERS. It has one function:

`run(repo, *args, read=False, check=True, text=True, env=None, inp=None, err=RuntimeError)`

**Default env.**
- Start from os.environ.
- Set `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`.
- Put `-c core.quotepath=off` in argv.
- When `read=True`, also set `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0`.
- Merge the caller's `env` last.

**Stderr rule.** On a non-zero exit with check=True, raise `err(msg)`. The message is:

`'git %s in %s exit %d: %s' % (' '.join(args[:3]), repo, rc, (stderr or stdout).strip()[-300:])`

The exception also carries `.stderr` and `.returncode` as attributes.

**Return value.**
- check=True: stripped str, or bytes when text=False.
- check=False: the CompletedProcess.

**How each caller keeps its own error type.** Pass a factory as `err`:
- cardrun: `err=StepFail`
- landq: `err=lambda m: EntryStop('FAILED', m)`
- canary, operator_run, land86: `err=Refused`
- clientrun: `err=Fail`
- opstatus: `check=False`, then return None when rc != 0.

**Order of the switch.**
1. cardrun: 28 helper calls, plus the 5 raw subprocess calls. Mark 1195 and 1444 `read=True`.
2. landq: 22 calls.
3. queue_build (862 `read=True`), operator_run (637 `read=True`) and integrate. integrate is not a checker, and today it loses stderr.
4. author, repair, pilot, canary.
5. opstatus, remote_build, clientrun, land86, evidence, triage.
6. Leave reclaim_plan and import_state as they are. They are sealed read-only on purpose.
7. Archive fix6_bench, but first do the L2 grep.

**Checkers.** Leave guard.py, proof.py, buildonce.py and toolslane.py on their own helpers. Move them only in a CHECKERS edit that is already planned, and then add gitx.py to CHECKERS in the same change.

**Fix the guard stderr loss now, at its callers.** These files are not checkers, so there is no rebuild:
- cardrun.py:1415 and cardrun.py:1553: when exc is a CalledProcessError, add `exc.stderr.decode(errors='replace')[-300:]` to the message.
- landq.py:547: do the same.

**Test.** Add `tests/test_gitx.py` with these cases:
1. A failing `git rev-parse nosuchref` raises the given `err` type. The message holds `nosuchref` and git's `fatal:` text.
2. A file named `é.txt` comes back from `ls-files` as `é.txt`, not as `"\303\251.txt"`.
3. After `touch` changes the stat data of a tracked file, `run(repo, 'status', read=True)` does not create `index.lock` and does not change the index mtime.
4. While a test holds `index.lock` (os.open with O_EXCL), `run(read=True)` still succeeds and leaves the lock in place.
5. Add `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` to the env check, with a fake https remote and a `fetch` that must fail fast.

**Expected gain.**
- 15 helper copies in non-checker modules go away, about 60-90 tokens each, so about 1,100 tokens in total.
- The env and error text are the same everywhere. All error messages name the git command and the repo, and they keep the stderr tail.
- The 4 live `git status` readers can no longer take `index.lock` while cardrun or landq commits.
- No card gets a new full_build or review, because the checker digest does not change.
- Risk: low. The run data shows 0 harm today (1 lock event, writer against writer, already fixed in ef285e73). So this change is a hardening fix, not an incident fix.

subject: ops
question:
After the drzero ops/2 fix, a backup failure after a done push only sets `backup_pending`. Is there a path that runs that backup again, and does a failed retry ever reach a human or stop the loop?

Path to check:
1. The sched path (a direct `cardrun land`, no landq): cardrun runs land_backup in the default mode 'run' (cardrun.py:1349-1368, s_backup at 1566-1578). On failure, sched.note_backup writes `r['backup_pending']` and emits one 'note' event (sched.py:519-525). grep finds no other read of `backup_pending` in sched.py, and no 'backup' text at all in operator_run.py. Does any code run sync.sh again for that card, or clear the flag? Or does the backup stay missing until a human runs sync.sh?
2. The landq path: `retry_backups` (landq.py:489-503) runs only in `Lander.run`. It runs after `quota.check` (landq.py:460-465), so it never runs in a pause. It does not run in `Lander.recover` (landq.py:562). It reads only landq entries, never the sched `r['backup_pending']` flags.
3. sync.sh has failures that a retry cannot fix: exit 3 from the size guard (state copy > 300 MB) and exit 1 from the key guard. `retry_backups` has no attempt count, no limit and no alert. Each landq run tries it again and logs only `backup-retry rc=N`.
4. `retry_backups` runs under the landq lock, before the first entry (landq.py:451, 465). `Lander.backup` calls `subprocess.run` with no timeout (landq.py:923-930). sync.sh waits up to 900 s for `sync.lock` (exit 4), and its `git push` has no timeout. So can one slow or stuck backup hold the landq lock and delay every land in the queue? Can a stuck backup do this with no limit?
5. Current data: /data/parity-v2/landq/queue.jsonl has 0 `backup_pending` entries and log.jsonl has 0 `backup-retry` events. So no real run has used this path yet. The canary backup is a stub that never fails (canary.py:284-285, 532-535).

Sub-questions:
(a) For each path (sched and landq), list who retries the backup, when, and how many times.
(b) Which sync.sh exit codes can a retry fix (4, a push race) and which can it not fix (3, 1)? Does the engine treat them differently?
(c) Is there a status line, operator stop or ntfy alert when `backup_pending` stays set for N lands or for T hours?
(d) Smallest fix. Proposal: one shared `backup_retry` in operator_run that reads both the sched and the landq flags. It runs outside the landq lock with a timeout. It tries again only on exit 4 or a push failure. It escalates on exit 1 or 3, or after K failures, and puts the reason in the operator status. Add a canary mode where the backup stub exits 3 once, then 0, with the invariant "every backup_pending is cleared or escalated before the run ends".
why: Lesson ops L4 moved the backup failure off the land result, but it may only have moved the problem. If the sched path never retries and the landq path retries with no limit, no alert and no timeout, then unattended runs lose backups without notice. A size-guard failure repeats forever. A stuck sync.sh can block the whole land queue while it holds the landq lock. The ops L6 lesson shows that the canary cannot see any of this, because its backup stub never fails.
answer: sched path: nothing retries the backup or clears r['backup_pending']. note_backup (sched.py:519-525) only writes the flag and one note. push_done (sched.py:510-517) makes the card landed, so cardrun never runs land_backup for it again. The backup only catches up when a later land runs sync.sh, which copies the whole state; the flag stays set. landq path: retry_backups (landq.py:489-503) runs at the start of each Lander.run, after quota.check (460-465), so never in a pause and never in recover. It has no try count, no limit, no alert and no timeout. It runs under the landq lock (451, 465), and Lander.backup has no timeout (923-930). sync.sh can wait 900 s on flock (:17), and its git push/pull/fetch have no timeout (:95-102). So one backup holds the land queue for 900 s or more, with no limit if a push hangs. Exit codes: 4 (lock) and 1 (index.lock, :86) can pass on a retry. 3 (size guard :48-53) and 1 (key guard :70-73) cannot. The engine treats all non-zero codes the same (landq.py:869-871, 497; cardrun.py:1359-1362). New finding: when both pushes fail, sync.sh exits 0. Under set -e a failure in a non-final part of an && list does not stop the script; a test of the same pattern exited 0. A push race is therefore never seen. Not being on main also exits 0 (:79-82). No status line, stop or ntfy alert exists: status_text (operator_run.py:1136-1150) has no backup field; a grep for ntfy/alert/escalat finds nothing; landed() clears r['why'] (sched.py:528). Data: 0 backup_pending in landq/queue.jsonl and 0 backup-retry in log.jsonl. A full scan of the sched/cardrun state.json files did not finish (the scans timed out), so it is not verified whether any real sched card holds backup_pending ❓. The canary backup stub never fails (canary.py:284-285, 532-535), and canary.py (f408e674) predates the backup fixes 758a9321 and ef285e73.
evidence: sched.py:519-525 note_backup only sets the flag and emits a note; sched.py:471,474,624 are its callers; no other code reads it (grep)
sched.py:510-517 push_done makes the card landed, so cardrun land does not run again; sched.py:528 landed() clears why
landq.py:451,460-465 lock, then quota.check, then retry_backups; recover at 562-575 does not call it
landq.py:489-503 retry_backups: no try count, only rc==0 matters, logs backup-retry rc=N
landq.py:923-930 Lander.backup subprocess.run with no timeout; landq.py:868 finish also runs the backup under the lock
backup/sync.sh:17 flock -w 900 exit 4; :48-53 size guard exit 3; :60 client_backup exit 3; :70-73 key guard exit 1; :84-87 index.lock exit 1; :79-82 not on main exits 0
backup/sync.sh:95-103 the backup-live fallback uses push && echo; a test of set -e with a failing && list exited 0, so a double push failure exits 0
operator_run.py:1136-1150 status_text has no backup field; grep ntfy|alert|escalat in operator_run/landq/sched finds 0 hits
/data/parity-v2/landq/queue.jsonl: 0 backup_pending; log.jsonl: 0 backup-retry; the recursive scans of the other run data timed out (rc=143, no match printed)
canary.py:284-285, 532-535 stub backup never fails; canary.py last commit f408e674 09:28 is before 758a9321 13:14 and ef285e73 13:36
proposal: Add backup_retry(op) in operator_run.py. Call it once per tick, outside the landq lock. It reads the sched st['cards'][*].backup_pending flags and the landq LANDED backup_pending entries. It runs sync.sh once with timeout=1200 s and GIT_SSH_COMMAND with ServerAliveInterval=30. Exit 0 clears all flags. Exit 4, index.lock or a timeout adds 1 to backup_tries and retries on the next tick. Exit 3, key-guard exit 1, backup_tries>=3 or more than 6 h pending sets heartbeat backup_blocked, shows it in status_text and sends one ntfy alert; lands continue. Remove retry_backups from Lander.run. Defer the backup in Lander.finish too, so sync.sh never runs under the landq lock. In sync.sh, make the failed backup-live push exit 5, and make the not-on-main case exit non-zero, so a push failure is seen. Add a canary mode backup-fail: the stub exits 3 once then 0, and in a second case it sleeps past the timeout. Invariant: every backup_pending is cleared or escalated before the run ends, and no land waits more than T for the landq lock. Gain: the sched path gets its first retry; the land queue cannot be blocked by sync.sh; exits 3 and 1 reach a human within 3 tries; push failures become visible; the canary covers the path.

grade.lesson: A failed backup after a done push is never retried on the sched path. The landq retry_backups runs under the landq lock with no timeout and no try limit. sync.sh exits 0 when every push fails.
grade.notes:
The main claims are confirmed.
- **Writers of the flag:** `grep backup_pending parityctl/*.py` finds sched.py:524 (writer only), cardrun.py:1361/1365/1368/1677 and landq.py:490-499/554/871. operator_run.py has no `backup`, `ntfy`, `alert` or `escalat` text (0 hits).
- **Call order in landq.py:** lock_dir at 451, then quota.check at 460-464, then retry_backups at 465. retry_backups (489-503) has no try count and checks only rc==0. Lander.backup (923-930) calls `subprocess.run` with no timeout. finish (868-872) also runs the backup under the lock.
- **sync.sh path:** the file is design/parity-v2/backup/sync.sh, not private-project/backup/sync.sh.
  - :17 flock -w 900 exits 4.
  - :48-53 and :60 exit 3.
  - :70-73 key guard exits 1.
  - :79-82 not-on-main exits 0.
  - :93-103 push, pull and fetch have no timeout.
- **Double push failure:** I reproduced it. `set -euo pipefail; false && echo x; echo reached` printed "reached" with rc=0. So when both pushes fail, sync.sh exits 0. This finding is correct and important.
- **One small error:** the solver says the index.lock path (:86) exits 1. It exits with git's own code. The `{ git add -A; exit 1; }` group is the last part of the && list, so set -e applies inside the group. My test gave rc=128.
- **status_text:** operator_run.py:1136-1150 has no backup field.
- **Canary:** the stub backup at canary.py:284-285 always returns 0. The settings at 532-535 use it.
- **Run data:** landq/queue.jsonl has 0 `backup_pending` and log.jsonl has 0 `backup-retry`. I found no sched state.json file within 3 levels of /data/parity-v2. A grep of sched* and operator* found no match. A deeper scan remains ❓, as the solver reported.
- **Proposal:** it is sound and small. It moves the backup out of the landq lock, adds a timeout and a try limit, and escalates through the status line and ntfy. It also fixes the exit 0 after a failed push. It should add: treat a rc≥128 from the index.lock path as a code that a retry can fix.

subject: tokens
question:
How many of the v2 author tokens (beq) go into function bodies that the /OPT:REF build drops? Can a reachability filter on the card scope cut beq per credited MATCH?

Background with evidence:
| Card | NOREF MATCH delta | REF MATCH delta | ledger beq |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| gap-06 | +37 | 0 | 2,953k |
| gap-08 | +32 | +1 | 4,514k |
| gap-04 | +30 | +1 (ledger says 13 pending, estimated) | 8,096k |
| gap-05 | +19 | 0 | 4,266k |
| gap-15 | +21 | +5 | 5,996k |
Source: gap-cards/gap-0{4,5,6,8}-result.json and gap-15-result.json `match_delta`, and `ledger.py report` (overall: 42.7M beq, 29 credited, 1,472k beq per credited MATCH).
- The REF build pairs about 842 LobbyDaemon functions. The NOREF build pairs 1,259-1,307 (gap-15 match_delta paired_before/after; gap-06 note "REF build pairs no card function").
- plan_cards.py already has a reachability model (`gains()`, plan_cards.py:251-263, and the `calibrate` command, line 25). The model says that a card with only unreachable bodies gets NOREF gain and no REF gain (plan_cards.py:883). But the author scope in the card md still lists all bodies, and the authors spend tokens on all of them.

Steps:
(1) For each metered card with a result file (gap-01..06, gap-08, gap-15, gap-int-1/2), list the card functions. Split them into 3 groups with the card's own REF and NOREF builds: (a) REF-paired at base, (b) REF-unpaired at base but REF-paired after the card (an unlock), (c) REF-unpaired before and after. Give n per group and per card.
(2) Give each group a share of the card's author beq. Use the session transcripts in REMETER_MAP (ledger.py:1118) and `meter.py session`. Attribute each assistant turn to the function that its Edit, Write or Read touches (file plus symbol in the hunk). Put turns that touch no card function into a shared pool and spread it by function count. Tell the attribution rule and its error ❓.
(3) Run `plan_cards.py calibrate` with the base builds of these cards. Find how well the reachability model predicts group (c) (precision and recall). Mark cards with n < 5 functions in a group with ❓.
(4) Compute beq per credited MATCH again with group (c) removed from the scope. Assume that the group (a)+(b) tokens and the REF gain stay the same. Compare with 1,472k and with the wave figure (206k beq per MATCH, docs/WAVES-VS-V2.md section 8.3).
(5) Recommend one concrete change, with its beq saving per credited MATCH: (i) the planner drops group (c) bodies from the card scope and puts them in a later "unlock" card behind the root that makes them reachable, (ii) the author prompt marks group (c) bodies as "NOREF only, lowest priority", or (iii) the repair and review steps skip group (c) items. Tell whether NOREF MATCH has any later value (does a group (c) body become a REF MATCH for free when a later card lands its caller?). Use gap-int-2 (29 credited, built on gap-01/02/03/int-1) as the test case.
why: The v2 ledger gives 1,472k beq per credited MATCH. The waves gave 206k. Earlier questions looked at the numerator: review repeats, cache_read, meter undercount, repair gate, planner unit and context split. No question looked at the denominator, which is the REF yield of the author work. The cards make many NOREF MATCH (+19 to +37) and almost no REF MATCH (0 to +5), so most of the author beq may go to bodies that /OPT:REF removes. The planner can already predict reachability (plan_cards.py:251), but the card scope does not use it. If group (c) holds most of the beq, a scope filter cuts tokens per MATCH more than any numerator fix. It also tells whether NOREF work is an investment or waste.
answer: About 82% (pooled; 71% direct-only lower bound) of the metered v2 author beq (31.8M of 38.8M) went into group (c) bodies: REF-unpaired before and after the card. Group sizes over 10 cards: a=28, b=11, c=356; every group b has n<5 (❓). With group (c) removed from scope, beq per credited MATCH falls from 1,472k to about 378k (526k at the lower bound), still 1.8-2.6x the wave figure of 206k. Two findings change the reading. (1) 28 of the 29 credited MATCH come from no card: a fresh REF build of d5b3dc3 already has 673 MATCH, but the Docs/Parity baseline has 645, and no src commit lies between the baseline accept (bc01acc) and d5b3dc3. The gap-int-2 stack caused only +1 REF MATCH (PacketFormatIterator::Reset). (2) Group (c) work is an investment: 110 of 225 group (c) bodies are REF MATCH in main ef90562 (1,451 paired / 1,151 MATCH). The gap-17 root stack turned the NOREF-only cards 04/05/06/08 into REF +105 (78 not MATCH in the gap-17-alone build). The ledger credits none of this to the cards that paid for it. On the base builds, the reachability model predicts group (c) with precision 0.97 and recall 0.95 (291/300/306). plan_cards.py calibrate crashes at line 1310 (a.no_calibration missing from the calibrate subparser).

subject: tools
question:
SQLite locks: are the shared ledgers safe and fast when many processes use them at the same time?

Facts from a short scan of parityctl/:
- No module sets `PRAGMA journal_mode`, `busy_timeout` or `synchronous`. A grep for these words in *.py finds nothing. So every database uses the default rollback journal (DELETE mode). In that mode, one writer blocks all readers.
- The lock wait differs from module to module:

| Module:line | Mode | Lock wait |
| --- | --- | --- |
| receipts.py:113 | read-write, autocommit | 30 s |
| events.py:91 | read-write, autocommit | 30 s |
| events.py:89 | read-only | 2 s |
| web.py:35 | read-only | 1 s |

answer:
SUMMARY. The ledgers are safe today, but they are not robust. The tests and the logs show this. Every write transaction in receipts.py, events.py, leases.py and pilot.py is short. Each is a BEGIN IMMEDIATE…COMMIT around 1 to 3 statements, and each does a ROLLBACK on BaseException. A bounded grep of 3,955 run files found 0 lock errors. The risk is in the design: DELETE journal mode, no busy_timeout policy, a schema run on each connect, and errors that do not explain themselves. A reader that holds its lock for longer than about 1 s stops all writers in DELETE mode. One test showed it: a 3 s reader stalled 4 writers for 3.07 to 3.45 s.

CORRECTIONS TO THE SCAN
- cardrun.py has 9 receipts.connect calls, not 11: lines 973, 1054, 1201, 1324, 1376, 1387, 1454, 1476 and 1510. landq.py has 5. review.py has 2 (816, 959). So the card and land path has 16 connects, and 14 of them are in cardrun and landq.
- repair.py opens the ledger at line 281, not 271.
- slotq.py does not open SQLite. A grep finds no sqlite3 or *.connect calls in it.
- The 'review receipts' are the per-card ledger.sqlite. review.py and review86.py write to --ledger, which is {ledger}=cardrun self.ledger (cardrun.py:147, 378). There is no separate file. The separate review-receipts.sqlite exists only once, as the old file fix3/review-receipts.sqlite.

(a) TABLE: FILE KIND → OPENERS
Legend: W = write, R = read, S = runs the schema on connect. ⇄ = can run at the same time as another opener of this file. ⚠ = the reader wait is shorter than the longest write hold. (No reader is ⚠ today. The longest write transaction is a few ms. The wait floor is 1 s.)

| File | Process | module:line | Mode | Wait |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| slotN/<card>/ledger.sqlite (receipts + review) | cardrun | cardrun.py:973…1510 (9×) | W+S | 30 s |
| 〃 | review.py / review86.py (child of cardrun) | review.py:816, 959; review86.py:654-661 | W+S | 30 s |
| 〃 | landq | landq.py:227, 585, 641 (read-only use, but W+S connect); 793, 842 | W+S | 30 s ⇄ cardrun at recover/adopt |
| 〃 | sched / operator_run | operator_run.py:714 → landq.review_handoff_plan → landq.py:227 | W+S | 30 s ⇄ cardrun |
| 〃 | integrate (land) | integrate.py:262, 320 | W+S, claim BEGIN IMMEDIATE | 30 s ⇄ landq |
| 〃 | ledger.py check / backfill | ledger.py:574, 1051, 1077 | R (mode=ro) | 5 s ⇄ all |
| 〃 | repair.py | repair.py:281 | R | 5 s ⇄ |
| 〃 | canary | canary.py:808 R; 257, 834 W+S | R/W | 5 s / 30 s |
| 〃 | score.py | score.py:98 | R | 5 s |
| 〃 | reclaim_plan | reclaim_plan.py:108 (ledgers + leases) | R | 5 s ⇄ |
| events.sqlite | sched | sched.py:255, 535 | W+S | 30 s ⇄ |
| 〃 | operator_run | operator_run.py:381 | W+S | 30 s ⇄ |
| 〃 | integrate | integrate.py:236 | W+S | 30 s ⇄ |

| 〃 | opstatus | opstatus.py:567 | R | 2 s ⇄ |

| leases.sqlite / cliproxy-worker.sqlite | pilot / worker | pilot.py:1259 → leases.py:12 | W, default isolation, ALTER on old file | 5 s ⇄ |

| 〃 | reclaim_plan | reclaim_plan.py:108 | R | 5 s |

On disk: 65 ledger.sqlite, 10 events.sqlite, 8 leases.sqlite and 9 pilot.sqlite at depth ≤5. /data is ext4 (findmnt). There are 0 -wal files. There is 1 leftover -journal: gap/review-04-stale/ledger.sqlite-journal, 8,720 bytes, header all zeros. That journal is not hot. A read-only open of a /tmp copy works and gives 0 review rows.

(b) SCHEMA-ON-CONNECT COST AND LOCKS
The test used a /tmp copy of cardrun/slot4/lift-lobbydaemon-gap-17/ledger.sqlite (311,296 bytes, 110 review rows, journal_mode=delete). /tmp is tmpfs.
- Median of 5×200 connects: a plain connect takes 240 µs. receipts.connect takes 4,393 µs. That is 18.3× slower and adds about 4.2 ms per connect. An earlier run gave 3.2 ms and 5.7 ms. The 16 connects in the card and land path cost about 70 ms for each card. This is small compared to a build, so the gain from the change is clarity and safety, not speed.
- executescript runs 26 statements. It runs no BEGIN or COMMIT, and in_transaction stays False. The file change counter (bytes 24-27) and the mtime do not change. So when the tables exist, it takes no RESERVED lock and writes nothing.
- A second connection held a lock while the first one connected:
  - Holder SHARED (BEGIN; SELECT): the connect succeeds in 0.001 s.
  - Holder RESERVED (BEGIN IMMEDIATE): the connect succeeds in 0.002 s.
  - Holder EXCLUSIVE for 3 s: the connect waits 3.056 s, then succeeds.
  - The same holder with a 1 s wait: OperationalError 'database is locked' after 1.009 s.
- Conclusion: a long reader cannot make a cardrun connect fail. Connect needs only SHARED. A reader blocks the COMMIT of the next write (the PENDING to EXCLUSIVE step). That COMMIT fails only if the reader holds its lock longer than 30 s. Today the readers in ledger.py hold their locks for milliseconds (110-row loops).
- Multi-process test (probe2.py): 1 reader held a read transaction for 3 s. 4 writer processes each wrote 200 rows (receipts.connect, then BEGIN IMMEDIATE / INSERT / COMMIT). 1 polling reader used a 1 s wait.

| Mode | Writer errors | Max writer wait | Polling-reader errors | Final rows | Reader saw a consistent snapshot |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| DELETE, 30 s | 0 / 800 | 3.07–3.45 s | 3 / 288 | 800 | yes (0 = 0) |
| WAL, 30 s | 0 / 800 | 0.026–0.058 s | 0 / 1,194 | 800 | yes |
| DELETE, 2 s (the writer does not ROLLBACK after an error) | 797 / 800 | — | — | 3 | 403 s wall |

The third row is a test artefact: my writer kept its failed transaction open. It shows what happens when a write path has no ROLLBACK. receipts.py, events.py:155-168 and pilot.py:826-834 all do a ROLLBACK, so they are safe.

(c) EVIDENCE IN THE LOGS AND ERROR HANDLING
- Search: find -maxdepth 4 over cardrun, landq, reviews, v2batch, ledger, gap, fix3b, step9f and canary, for *.log, *.txt, *.jsonl, *.json, *.err and *.out under 20 MB. It found 3,955 files. One pass of grep -E (xargs -P4, timeout 150 s) finished in 52.8 s with rc=123 (no match, no timeout).
- Results: 'database is locked' 0, 'database is busy' 0, OperationalError 0, 'disk I/O error' 0, 'readonly database' 0, 'unable to open database file' 0. So no example path exists. opstatus and web keep no output files.
- How the callers deal with an error:

| Caller | Handling |
|---|---|
| events.py:235, 241 (sync_receipts) | It catches OperationalError. At 235 it returns 0, and at 241 it skips the credit table. A 'database is locked' error is hidden here: no receipts sync this round, with no message. |
| score.py:101 | It catches OperationalError and returns set(). A lock error looks like 'no exclusions'. This is a correctness risk for the score. |
| web.py:82, 89, 101 | It catches sqlite3.Error and gives a 503 {"status":"Unavailable"} with no cause. |
| opstatus.py:87-92 safe() | It catches Exception and shows {'error': 'OperationalError: …'}. The text is visible, so the error is not fully hidden. |
| landq.py:232 | It catches sqlite3.Error and returns 'card ledger: <msg>'. The error is clear. |
| landq.py:646 | It catches Exception, logs adopt-failed, and continues. |
| ledger.py:581, repair.py:291, reclaim_plan.py:109, 119 | They catch sqlite3.Error. ledger.py gives a reason string. repair.py and reclaim_plan.py skip silently. |
| cardrun.py (9 connects), landq.py:585, 793, 842, review.py, sched.py, integrate.py | No catch. The process crashes with a bare 'database is locked'. The message has no file and no role. |
| Retry | None anywhere, other than the sqlite busy handler. |

- Test gaps: tests/ has no multi-process SQLite test. A grep for 'locked' and 'journal_mode' in test_receipts.py, test_chaos_receipts.py and test_events.py finds nothing. test_web.py uses a thread only for the HTTP server.

(d) WAL SAFETY
/data is local ext4, so WAL is safe for the live processes. backup/sync.sh:40-47 rsyncs '--include *.sqlite --exclude *'. That copies the main file only, with no -wal and no -shm. In WAL mode the backup would lose commits that are not checkpointed yet, and git tracks 109 .sqlite backup files. Today's DELETE-mode rsync of a live file can also give a torn copy ❓ (I did not test it). So WAL needs one change in sync.sh: take a snapshot with sqlite3.Connection.backup(), or run `PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)` before the rsync.

proposal:
Add parityctl/dbx.py. It is not in proof.CHECKERS (proof.py:63-65), and review_digest does not hash file bytes, so no digest changes. API: dbx.connect(path, role, schema=None, user_version=0).

1. Roles:

| Role | Open | Wait | Pragmas |
|---|---|---|---|
| reader | file:…?mode=ro, isolation_level=None | busy_timeout 5,000 ms (web 2,000 ms) | none, read-only |
| writer | isolation_level=None | busy_timeout 30,000 ms | journal_mode=WAL, synchronous=NORMAL; a helper `with dbx.tx(db):` runs BEGIN IMMEDIATE…COMMIT/ROLLBACK for every read-then-write (receipts.*, events._insert, leases.claim/finish, pilot.put) |
| schema | as writer | as writer | run SCHEMA only when PRAGMA user_version < N, inside BEGIN IMMEDIATE, then set user_version=N; also cache it once per process for each realpath |

Wrap OperationalError as dbx.LockError('<role> <path>: database is locked after <n> s'). Then a card step fails with a message that names the file and the role. Fix score.py:101 and events.py:235 so they catch only 'no such table' and re-raise a lock error.

2. Fix backup/sync.sh first, before any WAL switch. Snapshot each *.sqlite with sqlite3 backup() into the backup tree, or run wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE) before the rsync. Without this step, WAL loses commits from the 109 tracked backup ledgers.

3. Switch order:
   1. receipts.connect (this covers cardrun ×9, landq ×5, review ×2, integrate, canary).
   2. landq.py:227/585 → role=reader (they only read).
   3. events.connect (sched, operator_run, integrate, pilot) and the ro readers in opstatus and web.
   4. leases.connect (default isolation and ALTER → schema role with user_version).
   5. pilot.Ledger.
   6. The read-only tools: ledger.py, repair.py, reclaim_plan.py, score.py, client_backup.py.

4. Add tests/test_dbx.py:
   - One process holds a read transaction for 3 s while 4 writer processes each append 200 receipts through receipts.record_review. Assert 0 'database is locked' errors, 800 rows at the end, a reader count that does not change inside its transaction, and a max writer wait under 0.5 s.
   - A schema connect on an existing ledger does not change the file change counter.
   - Two processes run the leases schema upgrade on an old file at the same time, and neither gets 'duplicate column'.
   - A forced lock error gives a dbx.LockError text that names the path.

Expected gains (measured on a tmpfs copy):
- The writer stall behind a 3 s reader drops from 3.07–3.45 s to ≤0.058 s.
- Polling-reader errors drop from 3/288 to 0/1,194.
- Connect cost drops from about 4.4 ms to about 0.24 ms, which saves about 66 ms per card over 16 connects.
- A lock fault becomes a named error. Today it is a silent 0 or empty set at events.py:235 and score.py:101, or a bare 503 from web.py.
- The speed gain is small. The main value is lock robustness and clear errors.

grade.lesson: Run the schema of a SQLite ledger only when PRAGMA user_version is old, and before you switch a ledger to WAL, change backup/sync.sh: today it copies only *.sqlite files, so it does not copy the -wal file.
grade.notes:
I checked the answer myself. All checks were read-only. The only exception was a temporary /tmp copy, and I deleted it after the test.

What matches:
- `grep journal_mode|busy_timeout parityctl/*.py` finds nothing.
- The receipts.connect sites match the answer exactly. There are 9 in cardrun (973 to 1510), 5 in landq and 2 in review (816, 959). The scan said 11 for cardrun, so the correction to 9 is right.
- receipts.py:112-119 opens with timeout=30 and isolation_level=None, then runs executescript(SCHEMA).
- leases.py:12 uses a plain sqlite3.connect(path). It can run an ALTER TABLE on connect.
- score.py:101 turns an OperationalError into set(). events.py:235 turns it into 0, and events.py:241 passes. I confirmed all three.
- proof.CHECKERS does not include receipts, events, leases or dbx.
- slotq.py has 0 sqlite or connect matches.
- /data is ext4.
- The rsync in backup/sync.sh (the copy inside design/parity-v2) has --include '*.sqlite' and then --exclude '*'. So the WAL backup risk is real.

My rerun on a /tmp copy of slot4/lift-lobbydaemon-gap-17 gave:
- A plain connect takes 369 µs. receipts.connect takes 7,529 µs (about 20×). The answer said 240 µs against 4,393 µs (18×). That is the same order.
- With a SHARED holder open, receipts.connect finished in 0.0007 s.
- The file change counter did not change.
This supports the main claim: on an existing ledger, the schema run takes no write lock, and a reader cannot make a connect fail.

What I did not rerun:
- The multi-process WAL against DELETE numbers.
- The grep over 3,955 run files.
- The per-site table rows outside the receipts, leases, events and score modules (integrate, operator_run, canary, pilot line numbers).

Weak points:
- The sync.sh path is ambiguous. The answer says backup/sync.sh. The real file is design/parity-v2/backup/sync.sh, not a file at the repo root.
- In the third probe row, the test harness, not the system, caused the 797/800 failures. The answer says this.
- The ⚠ column of the table is empty. The answer explains why, but it gives no measured write-hold times. The "few ms" figure has no number behind it.

Value: the proposal (a dbx helper, user_version gating, a fix to sync.sh before the WAL switch, narrowing the catches in score.py and events.py) is sound and well ordered. The speed gain is small, as the answer admits. The main value is robustness and clear error messages.

question:
Does checker_digest cover every file that can change a proof or build result? Find each file outside the digest, show its effect, and design a digest that cannot drift.

Facts from a short scan:

| Fact | Evidence |

| review_digest hashes constants, not file bytes. x86_checker_digest extends checker_digest. | review.py:218-221, proof86.py:39-51 |

Questions:
(a) Find the full set of inputs for one proof: the Python import closure of CHECKERS, each script or module that the gate and build shell scripts run (follow the calls into bns-lift), each config key that a checker or gate reads, and each runtime patch from target.py. For each input, say whether checker_digest, pin_digest (PINNED in the lift tree), review_digest or x86_checker_digest covers it. Give file:line.
(b) For each input that no digest covers, read its commits since the first credited proof. Classify each commit: it can change a MATCH or verdict, or it cannot (for example logs or error text only). Give the commit, the file and the reason.
(c) Find the harm in the run data. List the proofs under /data/parity-v2/gap and /data/parity-v2/cardrun (use find -maxdepth 4) that were made before a commit from (b) that can change a verdict, and that the ledger credited after that commit. Give the count and one example. If you find none, say so.
(d) Find the opposite cost. cardrun.py:264 says one guard.py edit forces a new full_build and review on every card. Count the checker_digest values in the proofs, and count the digest changes where the only commit changed comments, logs or error text.
(e) Propose one fix. Options: compute the digest from the import closure plus a declared list of scripts and config keys, or hash the behaviour constants (as review_digest does) and keep a LEGACY list for edits that do not change behaviour. Say which module owns it. proof.CHECKERS hashes the module that holds it, so say how you avoid a loop. Name the test to add, for example tests/test_proof.py::test_checker_closure_is_hashed. That test parses the imports of CHECKERS and the script calls in the gate scripts, and fails when a reached local file is not in the digest and not in an explicit allow list that has a reason for each entry.
why: The integrate.py:189 refusal is the main guard against stale proofs, but it only protects the bytes it hashes. The scan shows 5 imported modules, 2 or more scripts called by the gates, the build configs and the target.py runtime patches outside the digest. Some of these files changed in November 2026. If any of those edits changed a verdict, old proofs stay valid when they should not. That is a false credit, and the earlier lessons about stale baselines and sibling proofs do not catch it. In the other direction, edits to comments alone in hashed files cost a full rebuild of every card. A closure-based or behaviour-based digest with a test fixes both problems and keeps them from coming back. This builds on [tools L6], but L6 covers only a new helper. This question covers the whole input set and its history.
answer:
## Short answer

proposal:
Fix: compute the digest from a closure, and do it in a new module, parityctl/checkerset.py.

1. Owner. checkerset.py owns the digest. proof.checker_digest() returns checkerset.digest(). proof86 and cardrun keep their calls.

2. What the digest hashes:
   - Roots (declared in checkerset.py): proof.py, toolslane.py, strict.py, cfgcheck.py, and the target gate scripts from targets/<t>.json (gates.fast, gates.ref, gates.noref).
   - The Python import closure of the roots, found with AST. checkerset.py is also in the closure.
   - The script closure, found with the regex that buildonce.script_files already uses, `(\$p|\$live|/parityctl)/X`, plus every file in each dir on the sandbox PATH (gate_shims/, link_shims/).
   - DECLARED_CONFIG: the values of targets/server.json gates, compare and binaries, and the build.json keys that reach a sandbox.
   - The patched proof.EXES and guard.CONFIG after target.patch_frozen.
   - Normalised content: the Python AST with docstrings removed, and the scripts with comment lines removed. A comment edit then does not change the digest.

3. No loop. checkerset.py stores no digest value, so hashing its own bytes is safe. The LEGACY adopt list lives in checkers-legacy.json. That file is not hashed. Each entry gives (old digest, new digest, commit, reason), the same pattern as review.adopt_legacy. Seed it with b50eece0 and 105fb472.

It fails when a reached local file is not in the digest set and not in ALLOW. ALLOW is a dict of file to reason, for example full-reference log: summary only, new_credit=False. Today the test would fail on atomicio, disk_guard, quota, target, uvsite, gate_shims/*, link_shims/* and build-noref.sh.
   - test_comment_edit_keeps_digest
   - test_fd_key_hashes_wrapper
   - test_legacy_file_not_hashed

6. Replace tests/test_proof.py:316 (fixed name list) with the closure test.

- 13 or more more files and 3 config groups are covered.
- The 20:07-01:47 class of drift becomes a test failure.
- The cost side stays the same as today or gets smaller: 0 of 9 past changes were comment-only, and 2 of 9 can be adopted through LEGACY.

subject: ops
question:
The engine has one global pause file (/data/parity-v2/PAUSE). It blocks model-free work for the full length of a model limit. A weekly limit can last up to MAX_PAUSE_S = 8 days (quota.py:47). A billing pause has no end until a human runs resume (quota.py:262-263). Does this pause stop work that never calls a model, and how much build and land time does that waste? What is the smallest scoped-pause design that stops only model calls?

Path to check:
1. Only model routes trip the pause. They are author.py:1320, cardrun.py:1081 (review), claude_route.py:72 and codex_adapter.py:60/255. The only model steps are author, cardrun 'review'/'review86' (and only for items without a receipt, cardrun.py:976-992), and repair kinds author/reproof/rebase (repair.py:1096).
2. But quota.check() also gates model-free work:
   - sched start: sched.py:323 and sched.py:674.
   - cardrun main, for check AND land: cardrun.py:1648.
   - every non-land step: cardrun.py:526. This covers plan, gate, full_build, lost_check, base_build, strict and proof.
   - buildonce builds: buildonce.py:282.
   - every landq entry: landq.py:461 and 513.
   - retry_backups, which runs only after the check (lesson ops L8).
3. The pause file has no 'scope' field (quota.py:3-5, pause() at 211-226).

Sub-questions:
(a) Classify each step in CHECK_STEPS + LAND_STEPS (cardrun.py:125-127), each landq step and each buildonce call. Is it a model call, or is it build or git only?
(b) In a weekly-limit pause, which cards could still advance? Examples: a READY card that waits in landq; a card whose review items all have receipts (cardrun.py:977-978) or that has no review items (cardrun.py:968-969); gate and full_build runs that warm the build cache for later cards. Use sched state and landq/queue.jsonl under /data/parity-v2 to count such cards at one point in time. Then estimate the wasted host-hours per paused day (build host slots in hosts.json × idle time).
(c) Does a pause that ends with many READY cards cause a land burst? Does that burst raise the integrate race rate (landq is_race)?
(d) Smallest fix. Proposal: add `scope` ('model' | 'all') to the pause record. trip() always writes scope='model'. A manual pause writes 'all'. Add quota.check(need='model'|'build'). Only author, review with pending items and repair-author pass need='model'. sched, cardrun build steps, landq and buildonce pass need='build'. A 'model' pause does not stop them. Questions about the fix: does cardrun need to split 'review' so that a card with full receipts skips the check? Does sched need a new phase, such as 'waits review (paused)', so that it does not restart the card's builds on every loop? Add a canary invariant: "in a scope=model pause, a READY card still lands, and no model stub is called".
why: Earlier lessons (ops L2, L3, L7, L8) asked whether a limit parks a card or uses up a retry. No lesson asked about the cost of the pause itself. Today one model limit freezes every build host and the land queue. A weekly limit can freeze them for up to 8 days, and a billing pause until a human acts. Yet most of the pipeline (gate, full_build, base_build, strict, proof, integrate, push, backup) calls no model. A scoped pause would keep build hosts and lands busy during a model outage. It would also stop the land burst at the end of the pause. The likely gain is days of build and land time for each weekly limit.
answer: Yes. The one global PAUSE file stops model-free work at 9 gates: sched.py:323/674, cardrun.py:526 (non-land steps) and :1648 (check and land start), landq.py:461/513 (retry_backups runs only after the check), buildonce.py:282, operator_run.py:420-440 (author, base build, check, landq run) and repair.py:1096. Only 3 things call a model: author, review run_review/review86 with pending items (cardrun.py:1110/1063), and the repair 'author' kind. Repair reproof and rebase are model-free: they run landq requeue or sched unpark (repair.py:1125-1134). Measured: 12,708 of 14,383 cardrun step-seconds (88.4%) are model-free. 26 of 41 done reviews (63%) had 0 items, so they called no model. At the snapshot (2026-11-26 about 15:26Z), 10 cards were READY, all with review items=0. All 10 could land without a model, but a pause holds them for up to 8 days (MAX_PAUSE_S), which is 80 card-days. Without the pause they land in about 40 minutes (land steps about 36 s per card from 1,041 s over 29 lands, plus a re-check of about 199 s, unverified). Idle host waste is small: 10 slots give 240 slot-hours a day, but the measured model-free demand is about 4 slot-hours a day, and authors stop in a model pause anyway. So the cost is land delay, not idle hosts. No pause has fired in production: there is no PAUSE or PAUSE.log, no /data/parity-v2/sched, and the landq log has only manual-landed and import-md events. A land burst does not raise the race rate. landq lands one entry at a time under one lock and rebases and re-checks each entry (landq.py:451, 726-740). is_race (landq.py:679) matches only main moving during a land, and there are 0 race events on record. The burst is a serial re-check queue of about 10 × 236 s. No review step split is needed: put need='model' only on the run_review and review86 calls. The --dry carry pass at cardrun.py:1150 is gated today but is model-free (unverified). sched must set not_before to the end of the pause, because today it restarts the card every 300 s (288 times a day). Restarts are cheap because the step() keys keep finished builds (cardrun.py:470).
